text:
Predicates:
GivenOut(x, y, z) ::: x is given out on y at z.
OnTV(x, y, z) ::: x is on TV at y on z.
OnShow(x, y) ::: x is on the show y.
Portrays(x, y) ::: x portrays the lives of y.
RealityTV(x) ::: x is a reality TV show.
Show(x) ::: x is a show.
Monday(x) ::: x is a Monday.
Time8pm(y) ::: y is 8 pm.
Premises:
∃x ∃y (Monday(x) ∧ Time8pm(y) ∧ OnTV(roses, x, y)) ::: On some Mondays at 8 pm, roses are given out on TV.
∀x ∀y ∀z (OnTV(x, y, z) ∧ x = roses → OnShow(x, bachelor)) ::: Every rose given out on TV is on the Bachelor.
∀x (OnShow(x, bachelor) → Portrays(x, realPeople)) ::: Everything on the Bachelor portrays the lives of real people.
∀x (Portrays(x, realPeople) → RealityTV(x)) ::: All shows portraying the lives of real people are reality TV shows.
¬RealityTV(breakingBad) ::: Breaking Bad is not a reality TV show.
Conclusion:
∀x ∀y (GivenOut(roses, x, y) ∧ OnShow(x, breakingBad) → (Monday(x) ∧ Time8pm(y))) ::: If roses are given out during Breaking Bad, then it is on Monday at 8 pm.
